newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury HQ may convert to luxury flats - sources.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury HQ may convert to luxury flats - sources.

text.p: Nothing is sacred, it appears, in the British Treasury's drive to get value for money in the 200 million stg redevelopment of its historic Whitehall premises.

Sources close to the Treasury said on Tuesday it was considering rival plans from two development consortia which have suggested the best value for money will be secured if the rear of the building is converted into luxury flats.
A Treasury spokesman refused to confirm the proposals but said it "would not rule out housing as an option".
With its prime central-London location and views of St James' Park and Buckingham Palace, there is little doubt any luxury flats would be quickly snapped up and swell the Treasury's coffers.
And the Treasury's local authority Westminister Council is known to be keen on mixed-use occupancy buildings.
The redevelopment will be a flagship project of the government's private finance initiative (PFI), the scheme to lure private cash into public infrastructure projects.

It will go to preferred bidder status in the autumn when the Treasury will chose the winning consortium and haggle over the final details. A final plan will be completed by the end of the year, the spokesman said.
The Victorian facade and central staircase will be retained, but the developer will be entrusted to replace the building's confined office space with more modern, open-plan working areas.

The site, just a kilometre away from Buckingham Palace and formerly host to the Indian High Commission, has not always had such a prestigious past. Last century it comprised a network of alleys plagued by pick-pockets and thieves.
